subject.title: [Feature Request] Hook Chain Integrity Protection Against Message Tampering

question: What hook-chain security model should OpenClaw support for mutable plugin hooks: host-owned audit/provenance for today’s in-process plugins, integrity checks across a future isolated-plugin IPC boundary, per-hook permission gating first, or some combination?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but implementing checksums, audit logs, or per-hook allowlists would encode a plugin trust boundary and compatibility policy that current code and docs do not settle.

options.title: Define audit and trust boundary first
options.body: Document the threat model, redaction and retention rules, and compatibility plan before changing hook runner behavior or config.

options.title: Ship redacted audit first
options.body: Add host-owned audit events for modifying hooks while deferring checksum enforcement and per-hook allowlists.

options.title: Defer checksum to isolated plugin IPC
options.body: Keep checksum enforcement blocked on process-isolation work so integrity checks are designed around a real boundary.

recommendation.title: Define audit and trust boundary first
recommendation.body: Document the threat model, redaction and retention rules, and compatibility plan before changing hook runner behavior or config.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already reviewed this as plugin-runtime security design and current blame points to Peter's restored-source ownership of the inspected hook/security files.
